event.transcript: Good morning everyone, and welcome to the conference.
Today I want to talk about how we are making it easier to build production-ready agents
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore gives you three core components: a runtime, a gateway, and memory.
With AgentCore Runtime, each session runs in its own isolated microVM for up to eight hours.
Last year, customers ran more than 1.5 billion inference requests on Amazon Bedrock.
We are also announcing Graviton5, which delivers up to 30% better price performance than Graviton4
Our new foundation models support a context window of one million tokens.
You can deploy inference endpoints across three Availability Zones to improve throughput and resilience.
With Retrieval-Augmented Generation, you can ground the model's responses in your own data.
Amazon S3 Vectors reduces the cost of storing and querying vectors by up to ninety percent.
Serverless inference means you only pay for the tokens you actually use.
Latency matters. Our customers expect a time to first token of less than two hundred milliseconds.
So what does this mean for your architecture?
First, start with a small evaluation set and measure before you optimize.
Second, use guardrails to keep your agent safe and compliant.
Third, monitor everything with observability tools like Amazon CloudWatch.
One customer reduced their deployment time from six weeks to four days
That is the power of building on a secure and scalable foundation
Thank you. And enjoy the rest of the conference.
All right, let's get started with today's lecture on machine learning.
Last week we talked about linear regression, so today we will move on to gradient descent
The idea is simple: we want to find the parameters that minimize the loss function.
Imagine you are standing on a hill in thick fog, and you want to walk down to the lowest point.
At each step, you look at the slope under your feet and take a small step downhill.
The size of that step is called the learning rate.
If the learning rate is too large, you will overshoot the minimum and the training will diverge.
If it is too small, training will take forever to converge.
In practice, we usually start with a learning rate of zero point zero zero one and adjust from there.
Now, who can tell me what overfitting means?
Overfitting happens when the model memorizes the training data instead of learning general patterns.
A common sign is that the training loss keeps going down while the validation loss starts going up.
To reduce overfitting, we can use regularization, dropout, or simply collect more data.
We also split our dataset into three parts: training, validation, and test.
A typical split is seventy percent for training, fifteen percent for validation, and fifteen percent for test.
Remember, you should never tune your hyperparameters on the test set.
For next week,
Please read chapter five and finish the second programming assignment.
The assignment is due on Friday at eleven fifty-nine p.m.
Any questions before we take a ten-minute break?
Hi everyone, thanks for joining the weekly sync.
Let's start with a quick update on the migration project.
We finished moving the user database to the new cluster on Tuesday.
The cutover took about forty minutes, which was shorter than the two hours we had planned.
However, we noticed that the P99 latency went up from 80 milliseconds to 120 milliseconds.
I think the root cause is a missing index on the orders table.
Could you take a look at that before the end of the week?
Sure, I will open a pull request by Thursday.
Great, the second topic is the budget for next quarter.
Power Cloud spending was two hundred and thirty thousand dollars last month, which is twelve percent over budget.
Most of the increase came from GPU instances used for model training.
We could save around thirty percent by switching to reserved capacity
Let's schedule a review with the finance team on March fifteenth.
One more thing, the security audit starts on the first of April
Please make sure that all access keys are rotated and that multi-factor authentication is enabled.
To summarize, we have three action items.
First, fix the missing index; second, prepare the cost review; third, complete the security checklist
Is there anything else before we wrap up?
Okay, thanks everyone. Talk to you next week.
